key_insight: For bounded-degree max-Ek-LINSAT over finite fields, the best possible approximation improves over random guessing only by about O(1/sqrt(D)), and this bound also frames what decoded quantum interferometry can hope to achieve.
engineering_relevance: The result gives a complexity-theoretic target for designing quantum and classical solvers on sparse constraint instances, showing that any practical advantage is likely to come from better constant factors rather than asymptotic scaling.
method: Prove NP-hardness of exceeding r/q + O_{q,r}(1/sqrt(D)) for bounded-degree max-Ek-LINSAT(q,r).
Connect the hardness benchmark to decoded quantum interferometry, QAOA, and classical heuristics on sparse instances.
Analyze decoder choice in DQI, showing classical decoders hit a 1/sqrt(D log D) barrier while quantum decoders can match 1/sqrt(D).
evidence_signal: The abstract states a worst-case complexity result over arbitrary finite fields and bounded-degree instances, with the scaling benchmark derived analytically rather than from empirical experiments.
watch_item: The DQI guarantee depends strongly on the decoder; classical decoding may fall short of the optimal 1/sqrt(D) scaling by an extra sqrt(log D) factor.
paper_title: Approximability limits for bounded-degree max-LINSAT and implications for decoded quantum interferometry
